abstract: The SMPTE progress report summarizes the key activities of the Society's technology committees, as well as the Standards Committee and other sub groups. The contents of this 2014 report demonstrate that there has been a lot of activity in the Standards Community, with a host of standards documents published in the past year.

authors.bio: Alan Lambshead retired in June 2013 from a career with Evertz Microsystems Ltd. in Burlington that spanned 34 years. In his most recent role as vice president, engineering, prior to his retirement, his responsibilities included the general oversight of R & D and product development, focusing on time code and post-production products. Under Lambshead's leadership, Evertz received the Philo T. Farnsworth Emmy in 2008; an industry recognition of Evertz' significant contribution to television engineering. Lambshead was instrumental in developing the first commercial devices for tracking film barcodes in the film-to-tape transfer suites of Hollywood and developing the end-to-end systems that enabled the widespread deployment of KeyKode throughout the world. This work was responsible for Evertz receiving an Emmy Engineering award in 1994 for its work on advancing KeyKode technology. Lambshead is co-inventor of “3-line VITC” and “Film Transfer Metadata,” both of which have been standardized by SMPTE. He pioneered the encoding of Film Transfer metadata into 1080p/24 high-definition video and has worked with other manufacturers to advance this technology for 4:4:4 digital acquisition for feature films, receiving a personal credit for this work in Star Wars Episode III—Revenge of the Sith in 2005. He led the Evertz team in the development of specialized HDTV products for 3DTV applications, and was involved in the development of Ultra HD products. During most of his time at Evertz, Lambshead actively participated on SMPTE Technology committees. He is the author of several SMPTE standards and recommended practices. He served as co-chair of the 32NF Network and Facilities Architecture committee from 2010–2013. Lambshead is a widely recognized expert in the field of HDTV time code and sync issues, HDTV production, HDTV metadata and has presented papers at local Sections and national SMPTE conferences. In 2013, Lambshead was elected to the position of SMPTE Standards Vice- President. In this role, he provides overall leadership to the SMPTE standards development process. As an elected officer of SMPTE, he is also a member of the SMPTE Executive committee and Board of Governors. Lambshead graduated from McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario with a B. Eng in electrical engineering in 1972 and became licensed as a Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) in Ontario in 1988. He became a SMPTE Fellow in 2009, and is a member of the Toronto SMPTE Section.
authors.name: Alan Lambshead

authors.bio: Paul Gardiner is standards manager at Sony Broadcast & Professional Research Labs, within Sony Europe Ltd., based in Basingstoke, U.K. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Southampton before joining the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) in 1974. His career has included a variety of roles related to the introduction of the ultrahigh-frequency (UHF) color television networks in the U.K. He has been involved in television technical regulation, and in R&D project management with responsibility for several international collaborative research projects. He became head of technical standards and information at the Independent Television Commission (ITC), the regulatory and licensing body for commercial television in the U.K. and subsequently at successor body Ofcom. Gardiner has been an active SMPTE member since joining Sony in 2007. He is a SMPTE Fellow and also a regular participant in the work of the ITUR.
authors.name: Paul Gardiner

authors.bio: Edward Reuss is an independent consultant specializing in video, audio and Wi-Fi networks, particularly for very low-latency applications. Earning an MSEE at Colorado State University, Reuss started in test and measurement, for Hewlett Packard (Agilent), Tektronix and Wavetek. He worked at General Instrument on the Eurocypher project for British Satellite Broadcasting (BSB). After several years developing scientific instruments at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, he was a director of systems engineering at Tiernan Communications, developing realtime MPEG-2 video encoders for DSNG and HDTV network distribution. Reuss switched to consumer products as a principal engineer in Plantronics' Advanced Technology Group, where he developed several advanced technology prototype headsets incorporating DSP, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. Since then, he has consulted for several clients, including GoPro, Intel, Clair Global and TiVo. Reuss is active in the SMPTE Standards Community. He is also a senior member of the IEEE and voting member of the IEEE 802.11 Working Group.
authors.name: Edward Reuss

authors.bio: Dave Schnuelle represents Dolby Laboratories as senior director, image technology, and provides guidance in Dolby's efforts in the television, cinema, and consumer imaging areas. He began his career as an engineer on television outside broadcasts while attending Purdue University. Schnuelle later held positions as chief engineer at various post-production facilities such as Editel and Modern VideoFilm in Los Angeles. Schnuelle worked with Lucasfilm's THX Division, beginning in 1991, where he was responsible for founding the THX Digital Mastering Program for quality-assurance of home video masters and duplicated software. As director of technology for THX, he directed research efforts into new technology for cinemas. During that period, he directly supervised the international digital cinema exhibition of the new Star Wars movies—Episode 1 (1999) and Episode 2 (2002). Schnuelle holds four patents on imaging and audio technology and has been deeply involved with film and television standards activities for 30 years. Schnuelle is a SMPTE Fellow and a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
authors.name: Dave Schnuelle

authors.bio: John Hurst is co-founder and chief technology officer of CineCert, LLC, an internationally recognized developer of digital cinema technology. Hurst has more than 30 years' experience in entertainment technology, at first in the practical application of recording and post-production, then later following his interests in product development. He has been involved in developing technologies for D-cinema since 2000. Under his direction, CineCert has produced several benchmark D-cinema projects, among them the Waimea KDM authoring system, the DCI Compliance Test Plan and the open source AS-DCP file access library. Hurst has developed many SMPTE standards for D-Cinema. He is a SMPTE Fellow.
authors.name: John Hurst

authors.bio: Mike Radford is vice president of engineering for 20th Century Fox. His responsibilities include both standards work within SMPTE as well as the design and development of critical production software systems in the area of Digital Cinema key management, mastering and workflow. He also represents 20th Century Fox on the Technical Committee of DCI. Before that he worked for Fox Television in the Advanced Engineering Group. There he specialized in RF propagation modeling and developed software systems to predict digital television (DTV) coverage and interference. Using the tools he authored, Radford participated in the design of more than 50 new Fox DTV broadcast facilities across the country.
authors.name: Radford Mike

authors.bio: Michael A. Dolan is founder and president of Television Broadcast Technology. He has been involved in digital television engineering for the past eight years. He currently chairs the Advanced Television Systems Committee Data Broadcasting Specialist Group (TSG/S13) and is active in the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA) and the Society for Cable Telecommunications Engineers (SCTE).
authors.name: Michael A. Dolan

authors.bio: Brian Vessa is a dedicated audio professional with more than 35 years of experience in the industry. After attending UCLA Engineering School he became a recording engineer, producing albums and recording orchestras. His passion was hot-rodding studio gear and discovering novel recording techniques. Vessa transitioned into film post as a music editor and sound editor, became a re-recording mixer at Cannon Films and MGM, then handled audio restoration at NT Audio. He was hired by Sony Pictures in 1998, and is currently executive director of digital audio mastering and representative to DCI. Vessa is a member of the Academy Sound Branch, SMPTE, and Audio Engineering Society. In addition to co-chairing 25CSS, he chairs the SMPTE D-Cinema and IMF sub-committees, and is the current chair of the DCI Technical Committee. He has written many audio specifications, including a white paper on near-field mixing for home theater, which has been widely adopted.
authors.name: Brian Vessa

authors.bio: Phil Tudor is a principal engineer at BBC Research & Development, London, U.K. He read electrical and information sciences at Cambridge University. Tudor's technical background includes software engineering, video compression algorithm development, MPEG standardization, metadata interoperability and the development of AAF and MXF standard file formats for use in tapeless production. Tudor is responsible for R&D projects in the areas of production tools, formats, workflow, media management and wide area production. Tudor is a board member of the Advanced Media Workflow Association. He is also a SMPTE fellow, a Chartered Engineer and a member of the IET.
authors.name: Phil Tudor

authors.bio: Paul Treleaven obtained a First Class Honours degree in electrical engineering from Imperial College, London in 1972. He started his career in broadcast engineering with BBC Designs Department. His work included design of the interpolation system for the BBC's “ACE” four-field standards converter. In 1979, Treleaven co-founded Avitel, a company designing and manufacturing video, audio and timecode distribution and processing equipment. He continued with Avitel as technical director until 2001. Treleaven is a member of the International Association of Broadcasting Manufacturers' (IABMs) Technical Task Group, representing the IABM at SMPTE and AES standards meetings and ABU technology committee meetings. He is also a member of the U.K.'s National Standards Body for IEC TC100. Treleaven has served as SMPTE International Region Governor and is a SMPTE Fellow. In addition to the SMPTE 30MR Technology Committee, he has chaired other SMPTE standards groups.
authors.name: Paul Treleaven

authors.bio: Pierre-Anthony Lemieux is a partner at Sandflow Consulting, where he works with both Hollywood and Silicon Valley clients on worldwide standards, proof-of-concept development, and product architecture. His expertise covers the entertainment technology ecosystem, from content authoring to playback, including audio and video and timed text, file formats, and content protection. His recent engagements include representing clients at industry forums (including SMPTE and W3C,) developing standards for file-based postproduction workflows and implementing audio processing algorithms. Lemieux is a SMPTE Fellow and currently serves as document editor in multiple SMPTE projects, in addition to chairing TC 31FS. He has a Ph.D. in Physics from UCLA and a B.Sc. from McGill University.
authors.name: Pierre-Anthony Lemieux

authors.bio: Thomas Bause Mason is director, advanced digital media technology, NBCU. As part of the NBCUniversal Advanced Technology Team, Bause researches and implements emerging technologies as well as standards for file-based workflows for production, post-production and distribution, including traditional broadcast, cable, and the Web. In addition, Bause works with various NBCUniversal operational teams, implementing standards and technology at the corporate level. Formerly, he worked at a major Hollywood post-production company where he built and ran encoding operations and supported business development with implementing new media workflows. Previously, Bause worked in Germany as a programmer, developing process visualization software and database solutions. He also managed a quality control department for several private broadcast networks at a large broadcast service provider. Bause has a bachelor's degree in media technology. He has been a SMPTE member since 2007. Bause served a two-year term as the co-chair 35PM TC and chaired the now completed SMPTE Studio Group on UHDTV Ecosystems.
authors.name: Thomas Bause Mason

authors.bio: John F. Snow represents Xilinx, Inc., where he is a video connectivity architect responsible for implementation of video interfaces in Xilinx field-programmable gate arrays, including SDI and HDMI. Prior to joining Xilinx in 2001, he was director of engineering at Evans & Sutherland where he was involved in realtime computer graphics for flight simulation. He has a BS degree in electrical engineering from Brigham Young University and is a senior member of the IEEE.
authors.name: John F. Snow

authors.bio: Friedrich Gierlinger is with the IRT, the Research and Development Institute of public broadcasting corporations of Germany (ARD, ZDF, DRadio), Austria (ORF) and Switzerland (SRG/SSR) since 1979. As an employ of the IRT he was involved in the development of different measurement techniques for analog and digital standard television for the public broadcasters and their standardization. Gierlinger chairs the German system and measurement expert group and is member of a working group of measurement and service department leaders of the Public Broadcasters in Germany. In the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) he is member of the Quality-Control working group as well as the Beyond-HD working group. In addition to co-chairing TC-32NF Gierlinger and is member of several other SMPTE groups.
authors.name: Friedrich Gierlinger

authors.bio: John Footen began his work in television 30 years ago. He attended New York University where he received degrees in film and TV production as well as computer science. He quickly combined the disciplines and played leadership roles in multiple manufacturing companies in developing products that used computers in media applications such as nonlinear video editing, video servers, and more. During this period the teams he led received patents and two technical Emmys for their work. Over the past 10 years Footen has moved into systems integration and consulting where he has an opportunity to address many of the real-world workflow issues seen across many types of media companies. A focus has been standards work around interfaces between software systems in media. Footen has co-chaired SMPTE standards activities in 32NF. He has pioneered the use of Service Oriented Architectures (SOA) in media, giving numerous educational talks and articles on the subject and originally co-chairing the FIMS effort by the AMWA and EBU. Footen has authored a book on SOA in Media and is a SMPTE member as well as a Senior Member of IEEE.
authors.name: John Footen

authors.bio: Chris Simons spent the early part of his career working for U.K. terrestrial and satellite broadcasters then joined Drake Automation Ltd. in 1996. As head of customer support, he established a global support infrastructure delivering major automation projects including BSkyB, DirecTV, Network Ten, SkyPerfecTV, Dish Network, and such. Following the acquisition of Encoda Systems by Harris in 2005 Simons managed the Automation Services organization covering both ADC and D-Series globally. After working at Miranda Technologies in 2006, Simons returned to Harris, now Imagine Communications, where he headed the Automation and Asset Management Product Group, responsible for the ADC, D-Series and Invenio product suite, before becoming head of engineering for all of the media product family.
authors.name: Chris Simons

authors.bio: Annie Chang is the vice president of post-production technology for The Walt Disney Studios. Chang oversees the research and implementation of new technology into Disney's feature visual effects, post-production and mastering pipelines. Her group focuses on improving the dailies, editorial, VFX, DI and mastering processes through new file-based workflows and standards efforts. Chang is currently chair of the Interoperable Master Format Working Group at SMPTE, which has been charged to develop the SMPTE standard for IMF. Prior to Disney, she spent six years at THX Ltd. as the senior engineer for the Digital Mastering Program and three years in DVD authoring and compression. Chang holds a BS in engineering technology from Texas A&M University.
authors.name: Annie Chang
